name: Planning Window Upgrades in Occupied or Rent-Controlled LA County Rentals

mainEntity.name: How should landlords in Los Angeles County plan window upgrades in rent-controlled or occupied units to minimize tenant disruption and comply with habitability rules?
mainEntity.text: How should landlords in Los Angeles County plan window upgrades in rent-controlled or occupied units to minimize tenant disruption and comply with habitability rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: For landlords in Los Angeles County, upgrading windows in occupied or rent-controlled units requires more planning than a single-family project. Start by mapping which units will be done on which days, ideally stacking work vertically or by building to minimize repeated mobilization. Provide tenants with written notices explaining dates, estimated time per room, and any temporary access limitations. Installers should protect interior furnishings with drop cloths or plastic and clean up daily, especially in units with children, elderly residents, or home workers. It is critical that each unit is left weather-tight and secure at the end of each day, with windows fully operable and locked where required. Coordinate with your property manager or legal advisor to ensure you follow local notice and entry rules for occupied units. In some cases, working hours, noise levels, and elevator usage may be regulated. Discuss with your window contractor how they handle multi-unit projects: crew size, daily unit targets, and communication with tenants onsite. Thoughtful sequencing and clear communication reduce tenant complaints, avoid habitability disputes, and keep the project on schedule.
acceptedAnswer.description: Landlords should plan window upgrades by coordinating schedules with tenants, grouping installations by stack or building, providing advance notice, protecting interiors from dust, and ensuring units remain secure and weather-tight each night. Work should comply with local habitability and access rules during the project.
